Hi Samir - great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking us through AcmeHealth's objectives. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can line up the technical review:

1) Data classification & PII: You mentioned that certain model inputs will contain PHI/PII and must not leave Acme's network for storage or processing unless encrypted and on a customer-managed key.
2) Retention & logs: Current requirement is 30-day minimum retention for application logs, but audit logs need to be retained for 7 years. Need clarity on what telemetry Redwood collects by default and whether retention can be configured per-tenant.
3) Data residency & egress: Primary requirement is US-only processing and strict egress controls. For the private deployment, you asked about fully air-gapped/on-prem options.
4) Network controls: You're going to share a network diagram and the list of approved outbound destinations/ports.

Proposed next steps:
- Please send the internal network diagram (vpc/subnets/firewall rules) before Fri 2/13 - this helps our infra team prepare the port/egress checklist.
- I'll loop in our Private deployment lead (Vivek) and runtime engineer (Dev) to run a short (30-45m) technical session next week to map data flows and enumerate what needs to be locked down.
- We'll provide a short doc on our default telemetry and how to opt out / configure retention.

Attaching a short dataflow primer for our Private/VPC option for your review (redwood-private-vpc-dataflow.pdf).

Thanks - happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,

Thanks Marissa - useful recap. Attaching our sketched network diagram and the list of security controls we expect (see acmehealth-vpc-outline.pdf). A few quick answers/clarifications from our side:

- We cannot allow any customer data to be sent to third-party telemetry endpoints for storage unless it is explicitly approved and encrypted with our KMS.
- For audit logs, we require immutable storage and an export path to our archival system - ideally via S3 compatible endpoint under our VPC (we can provide details).
- Air-gapped requirement: we are exploring a fully isolated on-prem deployment for a subset of sensitive workloads, but we would like to understand the installation and patching implications.

Can Vivek/Dev confirm whether Redwood offers an offline installer for air-gapped on-prem installs and what ports/outbound endpoints are required for Private (non-air-gapped) VPC deployments?

Hi Samir - thanks for the diagram. Short answers up front:

- Air-gapped / On-prem: Yes, we support an air-gapped on-prem deployment for regulated workloads. That path requires an offline installer and a short professional-services engagement to handle upgrades/patches and signing of binaries for your environment. We can provide an SLA and a maintenance window cadence.

- Outbound endpoints (Private/VPC): For non-air-gapped Private deployments the control plane needs to contact a small set of Redwood-managed endpoints for license checks and telemetry (optional). We can provide an allow-list JSON with IPs and hostnames ahead of the call. Typical ports: 443 egress to our control endpoints; optionally 5222 for agent heartbeat in hybrid setups. All telemetry is opt-in and can be disabled per-tenant.

- Audit logs & retention: Our Private runtime can write audit logs locally and we support periodic export to a customer-managed S3 or syslog aggregator inside your VPC. Retention policies are configurable; we support immutability via object lock on S3 or write-once archives for 7+ year retention.

- KMS/HSM: We support BYOK with cloud KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for on-prem. Enterprise plan includes a KMS integration workshop.

I'll bring the allow-list and a brief checklist to the call; if you can confirm which subnets will host the runtime and whether you prefer S3 export vs. syslog that helps.

- Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
